title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: A TWO-STEP COST SQUEEZE on the exact stack The Construct runs on: Claude Sonnet 5's promotional $2/$10 per-million pricing ends TODAY and standard $3/$15 takes effect tomorrow (a 50% input and input-plus-output increase), and on September 14 the Claude Code weekly limit boost expires for a NET 17% capacity cut — and `September 14`, `promotional pricing` and the 17% figure return ZERO matches across this corpus
bullets.summary: Two separate, independently sourced, dated changes land within fourteen days. First, Sonnet 5's promotional pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens ends August 31, 2026 — today — with standard $3/$15 taking effect September 1. Second, Anthropic's own developer account stated that starting September 14 it is permanently raising standard weekly Claude Code limits by 25% for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise, and that until then the current temporary 50% increase stays in place. Because the 50% summer boost (running since May 13 and extended three times, most recently through August 31) is being replaced by a permanent 25% bump over the ORIGINAL baseline, today's working capacity falls by roughly 17%: a 100-unit baseline became 150 under the promo and resets to 125 on September 14. This is reported consistently across BleepingComputer, Android Headlines, XenoSpectrum, Startup Fortune and explainX, all tracing to the same ClaudeDevs post, and the framing divergence is itself the story — the announcement says 'raising limits by 25%', the arithmetic against current state says minus 17%.
bullets.how: YES, and this is the most operationally consequential item this scan has surfaced in a fortnight, because unlike the Pentagon ruling or the memory-security literature it has a date, a number, and a bill attached. Both figures are absent from the corpus: `September 14` returns zero matches, `promotional pricing` returns zero, `weekly limit` appears once in seven weeks (07-02), and `17%` appears once in a July file about something else. The Construct runs Hermes, Lens, Mallard, Pulse and the PRAGMA operators continuously against these limits, and this report's own standing open item — six cost levers logged, none pulled, and a single `/cost` call on a long Lens or Pulse session still unmeasured after six days — has now acquired a deadline it did not have yesterday. The honest sequencing is: the price change bites tomorrow and is unavoidable, so nothing to decide there beyond knowing the run rate moves; the capacity change bites in fourteen days and IS actionable, because it is the difference between discovering the cut through a mid-session limit wall and knowing in advance which agents to move to cheaper models. The measurement that was optional last week is now the prerequisite: one `/cost` and `/usage` reading per long-running agent before September 14 establishes the baseline against which a 17% cut can actually be planned for rather than absorbed. Two limits stated plainly. The 17% figure was, at the 06:03 ET write, arithmetic performed by secondary outlets on Anthropic's own numbers rather than a number Anthropic published — and that limitation is SUPERSEDED as of the 10:00 ET re-check, because Anthropic deleted its original post and republished it stating the 17% reduction plainly (see bullet 5). It remains correct only for users currently saturating the boosted cap — a fleet running well under the limit feels a 25% increase, not a cut, and this report does not know which side of that line The Construct sits on, which is precisely what the unpulled measurement would settle. And the Sonnet 5 price change was carried once, on 08-25, so only the trigger date is new there.

bullets.title: Salesforce and Anthropic announced 'Claudeforce' — Claude embedded in the #1 CRM with Salesforce-in-Claude in pilot now and open beta expected in September — and the product name returns ZERO corpus matches despite `Salesforce` appearing in five prior files
bullets.summary: Salesforce's own newsroom press release, dated August 26, announces Claudeforce, positioned as a partnership putting Claude into Salesforce's CRM surface. The bidirectional half matters more than the headline for this stack: Salesforce IN Claude is available to select pilot customers now and is expected to launch in open beta in September 2026, meaning CRM records become readable and actionable from inside a Claude session rather than only the reverse. Logged from the primary corporate source rather than trade coverage. Stated as a limit: 'expected to launch in open beta in September' is a vendor forward-looking statement, the pilot is select-customer, and no pricing, no tool surface and no MCP details are given in the announcement, so nothing here is buildable this week.
bullets.how: MAYBE, and the interest is structural rather than immediate. `Claudeforce` returns zero matches while `Salesforce` appears in 07-01, 07-18, 08-01, 08-22 and 08-23 — so the vendor was on this scan's radar and the named product was not, which is the same coverage shape flagged repeatedly this week: the category gets tracked, the specific named thing that changes the buying decision does not. For The Construct directly the answer is closer to no — there is no Salesforce tenancy here to connect. For PRAGMA it is a genuine maybe, and the reason is the direction of travel rather than the product: when the CRM of record becomes addressable from inside an agent session, the operator wedge stops being 'we automate around your systems' and becomes 'we operate inside them', and every mid-market client conversation that currently stalls on integration cost gets easier. That is worth watching for the September open beta and worth nothing before it. The disciplined position is to log it, check whether the open beta actually lands in September, and resist the standing temptation of this beat, which is to convert a press release into a strategy slide before the product exists.

bullets.title: MEASURED aggregator lag, not asserted — the official Claude Code changelog was UNREACHABLE from this session today, and the summariser sites that had to be used instead report 2.1.247 (Aug 26) as the latest version when yesterday's run confirmed 2.1.251 (Aug 28) directly from the primary: four versions and five days of drift, quantified
bullets.summary: Today's run could not fetch code.claude.com directly — the fetch was refused because the URL had not appeared in a search result this session, a tooling constraint rather than a site outage — so this entry is explicitly a degraded-confidence reading and is labelled as such. What the searchable aggregators return is the finding: one changelog mirror states the latest version is 2.1.247, published August 26, 2026. Yesterday's run of this same report fetched the canonical changelog directly and recorded 2.1.251 dated August 28, with 2.1.250 (Aug 28) and 2.1.248 (Aug 27) beneath it. A targeted search for 2.1.252 again returns nothing on npm, the GitHub releases page or any changelog tracker, and the features the mirrors describe as recent — gateway spend-limit support in the usage warning, the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN 401 fix, the /model picker height fix — all sit in versions this corpus already carried. No evidence of any Claude Code release in the last 24 hours, and that is stated at the confidence the sources support rather than at the confidence yesterday's primary fetch supported.
bullets.how: MAYBE, and its value is that it converts a recurring hedge into a measurement. This report has said three days running that aggregators drift from the primary; today it can put a number on it — four versions and five days, on the single source this fleet depends on for its own tooling — because yesterday's primary fetch and today's aggregator reading are directly comparable. That is the first quantified estimate of the drift this corpus has ever held, and it was produced by the failure rather than despite it. The operationally useful consequence is a rule the scan should adopt rather than a task anyone must do: when the primary is unreachable, the correct output is the aggregator reading WITH its measured lag attached, not the aggregator reading presented as current, and not silence. Applied honestly today that means: the most recent Claude Code version this report can assert is 2.1.251, the mirrors are five days behind that, and no release in the last 24 hours is a reading rather than a finding. UPDATED at the 10:00 ET re-check: code.claude.com was reachable on the retry and the primary confirms 2.1.251 (Aug 28) as the top entry, with 2.1.250 (Aug 28) and 2.1.248 (Aug 27) beneath it and no 2.1.252 — so the degraded morning reading was correct, the null is now a finding rather than a reading, and the four-version / five-day aggregator lag stands measured against the primary itself rather than against yesterday's memory of it. The standing action is untouched and now seven days old — the version check against 2.1.251, no wildcard before a Bash subcommand, no machine setting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` — and it has now been carried unstarted for a week, which is long enough that it should either be done or dropped from the report.

bullets.title: NULL SWEEP, stated as a result — no frontier flagship, no new MCP server, no AI-agent funding round in the window, and the signage / wayfinding / permitting MCP negative holds for a NINTH consecutive day
bullets.summary: Four categories checked and four nulls, each verified rather than assumed. Frontier models: no release from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere dated Aug 30-31; the model trackers still show GLM-5.3 Flash (Aug 26) as the most recent, with Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 13) and the Aug 5 Meta Muse Spark 1.2 all already carried. MCP: no server released in the window; the newest items a fresh search surfaces are X's Ads MCP server (carried 08-25 and 08-28) and Betterworks v0.74.0 from Aug 13, with the Aug 22 MCP roadmap and Cloudflare's MCP v2 both carried across 08-15 through 08-29. Funding: the only agent-infrastructure round the trackers surface for this period is Sail Research's $80M — which is dated June 25 and was carried on 07-07 — with Baseten's Series F likewise carried; nothing dated Aug 30-31. arXiv: the papers returned on agent architecture and context engineering are 2603.09619, 2510.04618 and 2606.20683, all three of which this corpus carries across 08-24 to 08-27 and 07-11. And a ninth consecutive direct search for a signage, wayfinding or permitting MCP server returned only sign-industry marketing content — ADA renovation guides, NJ permit-cost articles, municipal signage-plan explainers — and no protocol tooling whatsoever.
bullets.how: NO, nothing here changes anything, and it is written down because a null that is checked is different from a null that is assumed. The signage negative is the one worth restating at nine days: the trade Brand 9 actually operates in has no agent-callable surface, nobody is building one, and every search for it returns marketing copy for sign companies. That has now been true for nine consecutive daily checks, which is long enough to stop being an absence and start being a fact about the market — and the corresponding observation is that whoever builds the permitting or wayfinding-spec layer first has no incumbent to displace. This report is not recommending building it; it is recording that the window has stayed open for nine days of looking. On the funding side the useful discipline is that the trackers surfaced Sail Research and Baseten as though current when both are two months old and both are already in this corpus, which is the same lag documented with a number in bullet 3, appearing in a second category on the same day.

bullets.title: The repricing that landed today carries a TOKENIZER CHANGE nobody costed — 10-35% more tokens on code ON TOP of the 50% rate rise, so a coding workload lands well above the headline — and Anthropic deleted and republished its Claude Code post to state the 17% cut plainly, converting this morning's hedge into the company's own number
bullets.summary: Two developments landed after this report was written at 06:03 ET and both bear directly on bullet 1. First, the Sonnet 5 repricing that took effect today is not only a rate change: it ships with a tokenizer change that adds roughly 10-35% more tokens on code, which compounds with the $2/$10 to $3/$15 move rather than sitting beside it — a coding-heavy workload therefore sees an effective increase materially above the 50% headline, and no bullet in this corpus has ever carried the tokenizer half. Second, on the Claude Code limits: Anthropic announced the permanent 25% raise on August 29, users publicly indexed the levels within hours (pre-May baseline 100, today 150, September 125), and Anthropic then deleted its original post and republished a clarification stating that against today the change works out to a 17% reduction. Two smaller same-day items from the same source, logged without a bullet each: GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 mini left Codex for ChatGPT sign-in users (still available via API key), and kimi-k2.5 and moonshot-v1 sunset today with kimi-k3 as the migration target. Stated as a limit: the 10-35% tokenizer figure is the outlet's characterisation and this report has not measured it against a real Construct workload.
bullets.how: YES, and it sharpens bullet 1 rather than repeating it. The tokenizer half is the genuinely new operational fact: every cost estimate in this corpus, including the six unpulled levers, has implicitly assumed the increase is a rate change and therefore multiplicative by 1.5 on the same token count. If the token count itself rises 10-35% on code, the compounded increase on a coding-heavy agent is closer to 1.65-2.0x, and The Construct's heaviest consumers — Hermes and the render-pipeline work — are exactly the code-shaped workloads that sit at the top of that range. That is not a reason to act differently, it is a reason the action already recommended got cheaper to justify: the single /cost reading this report has carried unpulled for six days now has a second unknown riding on it, because the same reading that establishes the September 14 capacity baseline also reveals whether the tokenizer change moved this fleet's token counts at all. One measurement, two questions, and a deadline. The Anthropic correction is worth less operationally and more as a check on this report's own method: the 06:03 bullet flagged that the 17% figure was secondary-source arithmetic and not the company's number, and four hours later it became the company's number. The hedge was correct when written and is now wrong, which is the right way for a hedge to fail.

praxis_lesson: This day ran twice, and the second run earned its keep by testing the first run's two hedges rather than restating its findings. Both hedges failed, and failed usefully. The 06:03 report said the 17% figure was secondary-source arithmetic and not Anthropic's own number; four hours later Anthropic deleted its post and republished the number, so the caveat was right when written and wrong by mid-morning. The 06:03 report also said the primary changelog was unreachable and published the aggregator reading with a measured five-day lag attached; on retry the primary was reachable and confirmed 2.1.251 exactly, which turns a degraded reading into a finding and validates the rule that produced it. The one genuinely new fact is the one nobody was hedging about: today's Sonnet 5 repricing carries a tokenizer change adding 10-35% more tokens on code, so the increase compounds rather than adds, and every cost estimate in this corpus has silently assumed otherwise. The lesson is the sequencing: a hedge is not a placeholder to be carried, it is a question with an expiry date, and the cheapest time to re-ask it is a few hours later on the same day. The measurement remains unpulled, now with two questions riding on it and fourteen days left.
